name: Cu Chi
dotReason: Worth it if you are already nearby
summary: Cu Chi is a district of tunnel complexes used by guerrilla fighters during the wars. The visitor site is a half-day from the city center, with a short stretch of widened tunnel you can crawl. It is a war-history stop, not a light outing.
getThere: 1.5–2 hours by road from District 1, depending on traffic
seoTitle: Cu Chi Tunnels — how to visit from Ho Chi Minh City
seoDescription: What the Cu Chi Tunnels site includes, how long the ride takes, and who should skip it.
intro: The tunnels at Cu Chi are a maintained visitor site over a much larger wartime network. You walk a shaded path, see reconstructed traps and living spaces, and can crawl a short, enlarged tunnel section.
Go with a guide who will explain the history, or read before you arrive. Shooting ranges on site use live ammunition and are optional. The heat under the trees is real; morning is kinder.
gettingAround: A private car or a group tour from District 1 is the practical way. Combine it with a delta stop only if you accept a very long day.

stayAreas.name: Ho Chi Minh City
stayAreas.summary: Return to the city the same day.

eat: Eat in the city. Site canteens are for a drink.
interestsBody: War history only. Skip it for children who will not have the context, and skip it if you have already spent the morning at the War Remnants Museum and need a different kind of afternoon.

interestGroups.title: The tunnels
interestGroups.summary: A short section widened for visitors. It is still narrow, dark, and hot.
